chunks.arabic_text: الكَافِي: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ، عَن عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَن أَبِيهِ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كُنتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الثَّانِي عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامِ إِذَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ صَالِحُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَهْلٍ، وَكَانَ يَتَوَلَّى لَهُ الْوَقْفَ بِقُمَ، فَقَالَ: يَا سَيِّدِي اجْعَلْنِي مِنَ الْعَشَرَةِ آلَافٍ فِي حَلٍّ فَإِنِّي أَنفَقْتُهَا، فَقَالَ لَهُ: أَنتَ فِي حَلٍّ، فَلَمَّا خَرَجَ صَالِحٌ، قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: أَحَدُهُمْ يَثْبُ عَلَى أَمْوَالِ حَقِّ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَأَيْتَامِهِمْ وَمَسَاكِينِهِمْ وَفُقَرَاءِهِمْ وَأَبْنَاءِ سَبِيلِهِمْ فَيَأْخُذُهُ ثُمَّ يَجِيءُ فَيَقُولُ: اجْعَلْنِي فِي حَلٍّ، أَتَرَاهُ ظَنَّ أَنِّي أَقُولُ: لَا أَفْعَلُ؟ وَاللَّهِ لَيَسْأَلَنَّهُمُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عَن ذَلِكَ سُؤَالًا حَثِيثًا

translations.en: I was with Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him) when Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Sahl entered to see him – and he used to oversee the endowments for him in Qum – he said: O my master! relieve me and do not hold me to account over ten thousand [Dirhams] for I have spent it, he said to him: you are relieved. When Salih had left, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: One of them pounces on the wealth which is the right of the family of Muhammad, their orphans, their poor, their needy, and their travelers – takes it [for himself] then comes and says: 'Relieve me.' Do you think he believed that I would say: 'No, I will not'? By Allah! Allah will surely ask them about that with a swift reckoning on the Day of Judgment.

en.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the specific category of 'Abna' al-Sabil' (travelers/poor) within the distribution of Khums and endowments, illustrating the Imam's pragmatic yet critical view of financial accountability. The Imam’s remark underscores that while he possesses the authority to forgive, the misappropriator bears the burden of proof and divine scrutiny, warning against the presumption that administrative forgiveness equates to absolution from God's strict accounting.
en.seo_question: What is the Imam's view on those who spend from the endowment funds of the Ahl al-Bayt?
